reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds in the shared refunds table match the three requested in this batch. I'll start by listing them.

The refunds table matches the three requested refunds exactly (orders 121, 122, and 124 with the same amounts), so I can proceed. Next I need the order list to identify the customers before checking their net balances.

The refunds table matches the three requested refunds exactly, so I can proceed. The customers are acme, birch, and cobalt. I'll get each customer's net balance before recording any payout, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 31368 matches its order total (5706 + 25662) with no refunds, so it is consistent. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 14737 matches its orders (8002 + 13081 = 21083) minus its refunds (5261 + 1085 = 6346). Cobalt is the last customer, so I'll get its net balance next.

Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus its refund on order 122 (5470). All three balances are consistent with the orders and the verified refunds, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout of 31368 is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout, which matches its net balance of 14737 (21083 orders minus 6346 refunds), and the refunds were verified against the batch.

Cobalt's net balance of 24286 matches its orders (29756) minus the verified refund on order 122 (5470), and that refund is in the batch and the refunds table. Recording Cobalt's payout is the last step.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its order total minus the verified refunds. Reporting the final payouts.
